dossier.public_summary: The 1.6-day, 15%-deep V-shaped dips are centered on the star and repeat every active-rotation cycle of the very spotted, slightly binary-looked M dwarf. At this size and shape the events are stellar eclipses, not planet transits, and the Gaia astrometric wobble supports a nearby stellar companion.

reasons.why: Undiluted size is stellar (rp_over_rstar 0.4175 on a 0.8725 Rsun M dwarf). A planet-sized alternative would require improbable dilution and still be ~39 Re, well above the giant-planet limit.
Highly V-shaped deep eclipse; flat-bottom planet shape disfavored at extreme significance. Fit bottom is V with best_ingress_fraction 0.45 and t14_h 1.749h.
Difference imaging puts the dip on the target (separate tool confirmed on 3 sectors). No plausible neighbour within 1 px can cause it: neighbours plausible_within_1px 0, could_cause 0.

Dip period 1.59d is identical to the star's spot rotation period (48043 ppm amplitude in sector 20). RUWE 11.8 and Gaia excess_noise_sig 2804 and rv_amplitude 32.61 indicate the target is a close binary/VR binary, so the 15% deep 1.75h V-shaped eclipses are stellar (EB or active binary), not transiting planet.

Depth changes 1.906% between sectors/pipelines even within TESS-SPOC (p=2.07e-25), not a calibration offset, as expected when a binary's dilution or activity changes with aperture, not a stable planet.
